result:
I've mapped the situation. Here's what's actually going on, and it's more than a typical "add some blog posts" task.

**What I found**

1. **The repo is missing pages that the live site serves.** `/features`, `/pricing`, every `/blog/post-N`, and the `/api/posts` endpoint don't exist anywhere in this repo (`app/` only has `page.tsx`, `blog/page.tsx`, `layout.tsx`, `sitemap.ts`). If this repo were deployed as-is, those routes would 404.
2. **Brand mismatch in the one piece of metadata the repo does control.** `app/layout.tsx` still sets the site title/description/OG to "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes," even though the product is now **Lumina**, an AI meeting assistant. Any page without its own metadata override inherits this wrong, old-product branding.
3. **The blog is broken for crawlers (and users).** `app/blog/page.tsx` renders nothing server-side and fetches `/api/posts` client-side — which doesn't exist, so it just shows a permanent spinner. It's also not how the live site's `/blog` works (that one has its own, different client-fetch-to-nowhere setup). Either way, blog posts aren't discoverable via on-site navigation or sitemap.
4. **`sitemap.ts` has a literal `TODO` leaving blog posts out** of the sitemap entirely — "once the content API exposes a stable listing" (it doesn't).
5. **`/faq` 301-redirects to `/#faq`**, but there is no FAQ section anywhere on the homepage. Dead-end redirect, and a missed FAQPage-schema rich-result opportunity.
6. **The GSC data tells a pivot story:** all 12 existing blog posts and most top queries are leftover **InboxZap** (email-cleanup) content — ~14,000 combined impressions but near-zero clicks, because they rank position 40–65 and are topically irrelevant to a meeting-assistant product now anyway. Meanwhile there is **zero** organic footprint for anything meeting/transcription/AI-notes related — the actual addressable market for Lumina isn't represented in search at all. The one bright spot: branded queries like `inboxzap`, `inboxzap app`, `inboxzap review` still convert decently (position ~4–8, ~4% CTR) — that's residual brand equity currently going nowhere since no page acknowledges the rebrand.

**Proposed plan**

- **Fix the correctness bugs** (rebrand the layout metadata, rebuild `/features` + `/pricing` + blog as real server-rendered pages in the repo, fix `/api/posts` or drop the client-fetch pattern, add blog posts + features/pricing to the sitemap, give `/faq` a real destination with FAQPage schema).
- **Capture the dying branded traffic**: add a short "InboxZap is now Lumina" bridge so `inboxzap`-type searchers land somewhere coherent instead of a mismatched/broken result.
- **Retire the 12 off-topic legacy posts** (301 them rather than leave them orphaned burning crawl budget for traffic that was never going to convert).
- **Start building real topical authority for Lumina** — a few new posts targeting actual meeting-assistant/AI-notes keywords, since right now that's a blank slate in GSC.

That's a fairly large chunk of work across strategy + code. Before I start building pages and writing new blog content, does this prioritization match what you want, or do you want to scope it down (e.g. just fix the technical bugs first, hold off on new content)?
